+
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+
+Repair the same acceptance gap here. The owned adapter inventories every window/tab
+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
+also rejects a changed handle set during inventory. Empty/malformed inventories
+and a missing inert tab fail. Existing PID/start identity is checked before native
+inventory; this adds no authority over a browser outside the owned adapter.
+
+Safari waits for the one navigation's observable URL result within two seconds,
+inside a five-second command bound; a pending navigation is never repeated. An
+inventory failure remains fatal and enters existing teardown. The inert page's
+script/worker/controller checks and strict storage deletion still follow this
+whole-browser boundary. No new product feature or broader framework is needed;
+scope remains L. Both reviewers must revalidate the repaired committed head.
+
+Added negative controls cover a background producer after restart, missing/empty
+inventories, unrelated origins, and navigation that never settles. The actual
+serialized Safari inventory script is exercised, including once-only mutation of
+the other fixture tab. **33/33 controls passed**, 300 ms including watchdog, peak
+91,328 KiB. Full lint/dependency/format checks passed in 16,916 ms at peak 766,704 KiB,
+with normal pressure throughout. These results supersede the pending tightened
+control/lint attempts above without erasing their resource dispositions. Hosted
+whole-browser process/native behavior remains explicitly pending.

+pressure level 2 after 3,251 ms, peak observed 1,360,048 KiB. No TypeScript success
+is claimed and no diagnostic was emitted before termination. Hosted Typecheck
+owns the remaining check; do not repeatedly load this Mac under pressure.
+
+During revalidation of `cef07957450cfaddc23014c1533131371b656a3b`, reviewer A
+identified a second fixture weakness: WebDriver handle order is not stable.
+Compare validated unique handle membership rather than ordered arrays, retaining
+rejection of new/missing/duplicate/malformed handles. Add the reordered-same-set
+positive control and changed-set negatives before final committed-source review.
+The [WebDriver specification](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-window-handles)
+permits arbitrary order. A scored this source 96/100 (35/23/18/10/10) with that

+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.

+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:

-# 🧽 SPN-141 Make native storage-loss preparation quiescent
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Operator](../product/personas.md#operator), I want native storage-loss checks to establish genuine storage absence, so that missing-copy recovery is tested without racing active cache writers.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### Storage-loss preparation has an observable settled boundary
-
-Given a native browser that already proved offline edits and reconnect,
-When the fixture deliberately removes its offline storage,
-Then active producers cannot recreate the removed shell cache during verification,
-And the subsequent offline UI does not advertise or open a missing retained copy.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Follow [sustainable testing](../testing.md); keep the Verify plan and progress evidence current. [Policy](../implementation/SPN-115.md#guidance-for-every-open-ticket-and-progress-checkpoint), owner 2026-11-01.
-- Preserve the [first Firefox failure, L scope and unchanged acceptance](../implementation/SPN-141.md#registration-and-scope), agent judgment 2026-11-04 after the owner requested continued SPN-120 repair.
-- Identify cache producers and establish an observable quiescent boundary before deletion. Do not repeatedly delete until green, loosen the empty-cache/targeted-database checks, add arbitrary sleeps, extend budgets or repeat failed assertions.
-- Preserve exact saved/offline/reconnect/conflict content and post-loss availability assertions. The observed failure is setup cache persistence, not demonstrated user data loss or a proven browser deletion defect.
-- Keep original private-database targeting and bounded diagnostic/cleanup behavior; unrelated browser databases are context, not required deletion targets.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Safari JXA process resolution (SPN-140), broad storage/runtime migrations, product features and SPN-120's finite historical audit.
-
-## Verify
-
-- Extend scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts and existing native harness controls for cache recreation after reported deletion, producer quiescence, denial/blocking/timeout and first-cause preservation.
-- Inspect service-worker lifecycle and controlled pages before choosing the boundary; retain full native desktop routing for all source/shared dependencies.

-- Preserve every run/source/tested identity, first failure, operation timeline, useful screenshot and both exact-source independent reviews. Mocks or retries cannot replace native proof.

+
+## 🧽 Leave active producers before deleting storage
+
+**2026-11-04, accepted implementation choice; agent judgment under the owner's
+request to continue SPN-120. Native acceptance remains pending.**
+
+The catalog effect in `web/offline/useOfflineDownloads.ts` explicitly calls
+`prepareShell` for retained downloads. That reaches the worker's `prepare`
+command and `fillRuntime` in `web/offline/runtimeCache.ts`, whose `caches.open`
+can create the shell cache. The original trace does not identify which invocation
+recreated it; this is a concrete concurrent producer, not proof of an OS defect.
+[The service-worker lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-service-workers-20261029/#unregister-algorithm)
+also explains why successful unregistration alone is insufficient: existing
+controlled clients and pending events can retain the worker.
+
+Choose a fixture-owned, same-origin inert document, with no scripts and a
+`default-src 'none'` policy. Navigate there after positively proving two available
+copies; this unloads the application's refresh/registration producers. Unregister
+workers there, retaining the still-present controller in evidence. Witness the
+existing adapter's graceful browser/driver exit, then reopen exactly that document
+through the existing `launch` function, which verifies the same profile and version.
+Only then delete storage, requiring the expected document, zero scripts, zero
+registered workers and no controller before the first storage mutation. The fresh
+document cannot start an application or worker. This is preparation, not a retry
+of deletion or of a failed postcondition.
+
+Keep one deletion request, the 28-second operation report inside the 30-second
+driver bound, the existing launch/stop bounds and 25-minute job bound. The separate
+unregistration request has the same 28-second bound and performs no cache/database
+deletion. Its failure prevents restart/deletion; stop/start failures remain fatal
+and flow through existing owned cleanup. Exactly one extra witnessed browser exit
+and same-profile start is expected per native owner. The final storage postconditions
+and all post-loss application assertions are unchanged. Other IndexedDB names remain
+diagnostics; only the private account database is targeted. No product path changes.
+
+Reject deletion from the active catalog, repeating cache deletion, fixed settling
+delays and broader timeouts. Navigation alone cannot prove that a pending worker
+event stopped; the owned restart supplies the additional lifecycle boundary.
+No general process or automation framework is added. Complete scope remains **L**:
+shared native fixture/lifecycle integration, negative controls and three-browser
+acceptance, with Safari's independent constructor defect still owned by SPN-140.
+
+Operator receives explicit preparation and deletion stages with first causes.
+Owner and Collaborator keep exact retained/reconnected/conflict content and honest
+missing-copy proof. Link guest access is unchanged. All four personas favor the
+strict absence check over accepting a cache that may still be populated.
+
+## 🔎 Concrete test plan and publication checkpoint
+
+`scripts/ci/desktop-storage.test.ts` owns deterministic serialized-script controls:
+the inert-document requirement, registration/controller rejection before mutation,
+unregistration without deletion, re-registration, successful deletion followed by
+cache recreation, blocked/retained databases, pending/rejected operations and a
+crashed driver with no diagnostic second request. First focused execution: **25/25
+passed**, 323 ms including watchdog, peak 92,560 KiB, normal memory pressure.
+It does not prove browser process lifetimes or native acceptance.
+
+The existing Desktop offline workflow owns that integration. Before publishing,
+declare **one first-attempt workflow triggered by this candidate's PR opening**:
+Chrome and Firefox on macOS 26, Safari on macOS 15 Intel, unchanged owners and
+25-minute bounds. Expect the original exact content/images/reconnect/conflict
+checks, inert preparation and unregistration, a fourth same-profile launch/exit,
+strict empty-storage proof and both post-loss assertions for every owner. Safari
+must also pass the unchanged capability sentinel/identity/baseline checks. Preserve
+any first failure; no unchanged rerun or automatic renewal is part of this plan.
+
+All changed runtime/test files are under `scripts/ci/desktop-*.ts`, already selected
+by the native workflow. Ordinary unknown script paths conservatively select full
+CI; no routing, assertion, retry or applicability change is needed. Full constrained
+typecheck and lint, backlog/index/PR validation and two independent committed-source
+grades precede publication. Hosted ordinary gates and selected native evidence
+remain pending until observed on the exact source/tested identities.
+
+Local constrained typecheck was **resource-aborted**, not passed: the watchdog
+observed macOS pressure level 2 after 1,706 ms at 1,296,288 KiB. Subsequent
+format/focused-control/lint launches were refused at pressure 2. The first 25-test
+pass predates only a tighter asynchronous cache-recreation control and formatting;
+that refinement requires a fresh run when pressure is normal. Retain both results.
+
+## 🏁 Prepared landing bookkeeping
+
+Delete SPN-141's ticket, remove its dependency from SPN-120, append its completion
+counter and regenerate the index in this candidate. These are prepared landing
+changes; they do not declare pending native acceptance complete. SPN-140 and
+SPN-120 retain their own full obligations. Final run identities, measured results,
+both exact-source reviews and failure dispositions belong in the PR description
+or immutable maintained evidence before obsolete branches are removed.
+
+## 🔎 Independent review repair: restored background clients
+
+Both nonimplementing reviewers rejected candidate
+`14147960accca0927f0b61dfd4c66b7de98685ec`: A **94/100** (35/20/19/10/10),
+B **92/100** (31/23/18/10/10). Their shared P2 finding was concrete: the existing
+Safari adapter permits restored background tabs, so checking the selected inert
+document alone does not establish producer quiescence. No validation push occurred.
+

+(Safari) or WebDriver window handle (Chrome/Firefox). Before unregistration, navigate
+other tabs on this exact fixture origin to the inert URL once; leave unrelated
+origins unchanged. Retain before/after URL inventories. After the witnessed restart,
+inventory again in read-only mode and reject any fixture-origin URL other than the
+inert document; do not navigate a newly restored producer and proceed. WebDriver
